neurips-2024-cofie-learning-compact-neur.tldr: CoFie aligns local coordinate frames to represent unseen 3D surfaces more compactly.
paragraphs: A local surface patch can be simpler to describe when its coordinates align with its normal and tangent directions. CoFie uses this observation, motivated by a quadratic analysis of local signed-distance functions, to improve neural surface representations.

An optimizable Coordinate Field transforms local shapes from world coordinates into aligned local frames. Quadratic layers in the multilayer perceptron further strengthen its ability to represent local geometry. The model is trained on a curated shape collection and then applied to new shape instances.

At the same parameter count as earlier methods, CoFie reduces shape error by 48% for novel instances of training categories and 56% for unseen categories. It also matches prior performance with 70% fewer parameters. These results concern the evaluated shape collections; the abstract does not specify the error metric or establish equal compression gains for every surface family.

neurips-2024-efficient-policy-evaluation.tldr: Graphical criteria and estimators combine experiments from multiple sites to evaluate target policies.
paragraphs: Policy evaluation often combines data from studies conducted in different settings. If their distributions differ from the intended deployment population, treating all observations as interchangeable can produce misleading effect estimates. This paper addresses transportability as well as estimation from finite samples.

The authors develop graphical criteria and estimators for evaluating conditional and stochastic policies using multiple experimental datasets. The aim is to exploit what each study reveals while accounting for the relationships between source sites and the target setting.

An asymptotic error analysis provides fast-convergence guarantees, and simulations test estimator robustness. The abstract does not list the graphical assumptions or numerical error reductions. Its contribution is a framework for justified data combination under specified causal structure, rather than the claim that pooling heterogeneous experiments automatically gives an unbiased estimate of any policy’s effect in a new population.

neurips-2024-em-distillation-for-one-ste.tldr: EM Distillation turns diffusion teachers into one-step generators using a maximum-likelihood formulation.
paragraphs: Diffusion models generate high-quality samples through an expensive iterative process. Distilling them into one-step generators can reduce cost but may lose quality or miss parts of the distribution. EM Distillation, or EMD, approaches this task through maximum likelihood and expectation-maximization.

The generator updates use samples from a joint distribution involving the diffusion teacher’s prior and inferred generator latents. A reparameterized sampling scheme and noise cancellation stabilize the procedure. The authors also connect the formulation with existing approaches based on mode-seeking KL minimization.

EMD improves FID over prior one-step generators on ImageNet-64 and ImageNet-128 and compares favorably on text-to-image distillation. The abstract does not give absolute FID values or all data-access requirements. The contribution is a distribution-oriented distillation objective and stabilization method, with evidence that one-step sampling can retain stronger perceptual quality in the evaluated systems.

neurips-2024-error-correction-output-cod.tldr: Neural-tangent-kernel analysis guides error-correcting output codes for networks with weight errors.
paragraphs: One-hot class codes are simple but offer limited protection when a network’s weights are corrupted. This paper analyzes alternative error-correcting output codes to connect code design with architecture, perturbation magnitude, and robust classification accuracy.

Through the neural tangent kernel, the authors show that changing from one-hot to other codes corresponds, in clean models, to changing decoding from Euclidean to Mahalanobis distance. With weight errors, an architecture-dependent normalized-distance threshold permits recovery of clean accuracy as code length tends to infinity.

These results guide practical codes by balancing orthogonality against separation between codewords, with different choices for simpler and more complex tasks. Experiments across four datasets and four architectures outperform existing codes. The asymptotic guarantee should not be mistaken for exact robustness of every finite code; the practical experiments and infinite-length theorem provide different kinds of evidence.

neurips-2024-expert-level-protocol-trans.tldr: A three-stage translation workflow converts human laboratory protocols into structured dependence graphs.
paragraphs: Laboratory protocols written for people often rely on tacit knowledge and informal sequencing. Automated laboratories need explicit operations whose dependencies remain consistent. This paper targets the translation step that otherwise requires labor-intensive collaboration between domain experts and software specialists.

The proposed workflow incrementally builds Protocol Dependence Graphs in three stages. It first structures syntax, then completes semantic information, and finally links execution-level relationships, aiming to preserve causality and consistency across the protocol’s steps.

Quantitative and qualitative evaluations find performance comparable to human experts. The abstract does not identify the scientific domains, evaluation metrics, or the extent of physical execution testing. The supported contribution is automated protocol translation with expert-level evaluated quality, rather than evidence that every translated procedure can be executed autonomously without further validation in a self-driving laboratory.

neurips-2024-exploring-fixed-point-in-im.tldr: Fixed-point analysis improves DDIM inversion and supports an unsupervised dehazing application.
paragraphs: DDIM inversion maps an image back to a noise representation so that editing can preserve unmodified content. Approximating one timestep’s noise prediction with another introduces reconstruction errors. Recent methods reduce these errors by casting each inversion step as a fixed-point problem, but their theoretical basis was incomplete.

This paper studies the existence of those fixed points and uses the resulting theory to optimize a convergence-oriented loss for inversion. The objective is to reconstruct the reference image more faithfully and improve the visual quality of subsequent edits.

The authors also extend fixed-point-based editing to text-based unsupervised image dehazing. The abstract does not provide quantitative reconstruction, editing, or dehazing results, nor does it state the exact existence assumptions. The contribution connects a practical inversion technique to mathematical support and uses that connection to refine the editing procedure and explore a related restoration task.

neurips-2024-frustratingly-easy-test-tim.tldr: ZERO adapts vision-language predictions through augmented-view voting without backpropagation.
paragraphs: Test-time adaptation can improve a vision-language model’s response to a single difficult unlabeled image, but prompt tuning adds inference time and memory through online backpropagation. This paper analyzes entropy-minimization-based adaptation and extracts a simpler prediction procedure.

ZERO creates multiple augmented views, predicts their classes, retains the most confident predictions, and marginalizes after setting softmax temperature to zero. It requires one batched forward pass through the vision encoder and no backward passes.

Under established evaluation protocols, ZERO surpasses or compares favorably with state-of-the-art methods while running almost 10x faster and using about 13x less memory than standard test-time prompt tuning. The abstract does not give dataset-level accuracies. Its contribution is a strong low-overhead baseline for the studied episodic adaptation setting, rather than a learned parameter update or a guarantee of improvement on every individual image.

neurips-2024-gacl-exemplar-free-generali.tldr: GACL gives exemplar-free analytic updates equivalent to joint training within its continual-learning formulation.
paragraphs: Generalized class-incremental learning receives mixed categories with unknown sample-size distributions across incoming tasks. This makes forgetting and uneven task composition difficult to manage. GACL addresses the setting without retaining exemplar data from earlier tasks.

The method uses gradient-free analytic learning to derive a closed-form update. It separates incoming examples into previously exposed and new classes, obtaining a weight-invariance property that supports equivalence between incremental updates and joint training in the proposed formulation. Matrix analysis establishes that equivalence.

Across multiple datasets and generalized continual-learning settings, GACL consistently leads the evaluated alternatives. The abstract does not report accuracy values or assert equivalence for arbitrary neural-network training procedures. Its no-exemplar design reduces reliance on stored historical samples, but the contribution described is learning behavior and storage practice, not a formal privacy guarantee for all retained model information.

neurips-2024-graph-structure-inference-w.tldr: Bilinear attention over covariance geometry supports rapid inference of variable-dependence graphs.
paragraphs: Inferring relationships among observed variables is central to many scientific analyses. This paper trains a neural model to map observational datasets directly to dependence structures, using simulated training data with varying shapes and couplings. Inference then requires only a single forward pass.

The central bilinear attention mechanism operates on covariance matrices of transformed data while respecting symmetric-positive-definite geometry. Inspired by graphical lasso, the model uses continuous graph representations in a space where inverse covariance encodes conditional independence.

Experiments show strong undirected-graph estimation, robustness across dependencies, and competitive completed-partially-directed-acyclic-graph estimation through a two-step approach. The abstract also reports generalization across nonlinear functional forms. It does not spell out causal-identification assumptions; observational dependence estimates should not be read as unrestricted proof of causal direction without the conditions underlying the evaluated graph-inference setting.

neurips-2024-id-to-3d-expressive-id-guid.tldr: ID-to-3D generates identity-guided, expression-controllable 3D heads from minimal image input.
paragraphs: Creating a detailed three-dimensional head from a casually captured photograph requires separating identity, expression, geometry, and appearance. ID-to-3D combines identity and text guidance with task-specific two-dimensional diffusion priors to generate heads even from a single image.

A lightweight identity-aware and expression-aware extension fine-tunes only 0.2% of a foundation model’s available training parameters. The system combines a neural parametric expression representation with multistage geometry and albedo generation, aiming to capture facial features, hair, and accessories.

The outputs can be converted to render-ready meshes, and the authors report high-quality, identity-consistent results on unseen identities without large captured three-dimensional human datasets. The abstract supplies no numerical identity or geometry metrics. The contribution is a compositional generation pipeline and demonstrated visual quality, rather than verified exact recovery of a subject’s hidden anatomy from one photograph.

neurips-2024-identifiability-guarantees-.tldr: Observational causal disentanglement has a precise layer-wise identifiability limit in the studied model class.
paragraphs: Causal representation learning often assumes access to interventions on hidden factors, an assumption difficult to satisfy in practice. This paper asks what purely observational data can identify when latent causal dynamics are nonlinear with additive Gaussian noise and observations use linear mixing.

The authors characterize identifiable factors without interventions or restrictions on the causal graph. Variables are recoverable up to a layer-wise transformation, and further disentanglement is shown to be impossible in this setting. The limit is as important as the positive result.

A practical algorithm solves a quadratic program based on estimated scores of the observed distribution. Simulations support the guarantees and show meaningful recovered representations. The abstract does not provide experimental metrics. Its conclusions depend on the specified noise and mixing model, rather than proving unrestricted recovery of hidden causal variables from arbitrary observational measurements.

neurips-2024-in-context-learning-with-tr.tldr: Softmax attention learns a task-adapted neighborhood predictor for in-context regression.
paragraphs: In-context learning asks a model to adapt to a new task from examples provided at inference, without changing its parameters. This paper examines how a softmax attention unit supports that behavior when each context describes a regression problem.

The analysis shows that attention learns a window implementing a nearest-neighbor-style predictor tuned to the pretraining tasks. The window broadens when functions are less Lipschitz or label noise increases. For low-rank linear problems, the unit first learns to project into the relevant subspace.

This adaptivity relies on softmax and cannot be reproduced by the linear activation considered in several earlier theoretical analyses. The abstract does not claim this simple unit explains every component of full-scale language-model in-context learning. Its contribution is a concrete mechanism showing why the nonlinear attention function matters for adaptation in the studied regression setting.

neurips-2024-in-trajectory-inverse-reinf.tldr: In-trajectory inverse reinforcement learning updates rewards and policies before a demonstration finishes.
paragraphs: Inverse reinforcement learning usually waits for completed expert trajectories before estimating a reward and policy. This paper instead begins with the first observed state-action pair and updates incrementally as the same ongoing trajectory reveals additional steps.

The problem is formulated as online bilevel optimization. The upper level adjusts the inferred reward using each new observation and a meta-regularization term; the lower level learns the policy corresponding to that reward. This couples evolving reward estimation with policy improvement during the demonstration.

The proposed algorithm has sublinear local regret O(sqrt(T) + log(T) + sqrt(T) log(T)). With a linear reward function, the authors prove O(log(T)) regret. Experiments validate the method, although the abstract supplies no numerical results. The general local-regret guarantee and the stronger linear-reward statement apply to different conditions and should not be treated as interchangeable.

neurips-2024-learning-general-parameteri.tldr: Primal-dual policy gradients receive regret and constraint-violation bounds for average-reward constrained control.
paragraphs: Infinite-horizon constrained Markov decision processes balance long-run reward with restrictions on behavior. This paper studies average reward with a general parameterized policy, asking how performance shortfall and constraint violations accumulate during learning rather than only analyzing a final policy.

The authors propose a primal-dual policy-gradient algorithm. The formulation manages the reward objective and constraints together, with the stated aim of approaching a globally optimal policy while keeping cumulative regret and violations controlled.

The reported bounds are approximately O(T^(4/5)) for both objective regret and constraint violation, up to logarithmic factors. Since these grow sublinearly, their per-step averages diminish under the analysis. The abstract does not state the full assumptions, policy-approximation conditions, or empirical results. The contribution is a theoretical extension to this average-reward setting, not a claim that constraints are never violated at any individual learning step.

neurips-2024-learning-rigid-body-simulat.tldr: SDF-Sim replaces mesh-heavy collision processing with implicit geometry to scale learned rigid-body simulation.
paragraphs: Learned graph-network simulators can model rigid-body interactions, but detailed meshes and many objects make collision handling expensive. SDF-Sim represents object shapes using learned signed-distance functions and designs the simulator around those representations to avoid a central mesh-based bottleneck.

The implicit shape representation accelerates distance computation while preserving a graph-based learned dynamics model. The paper targets scenes with large object counts and complex geometry, where previous mesh-based learned simulators exhaust available memory.

Demonstrations scale to hundreds of objects and up to 1.1 million nodes. The method also handles real-world scenes by extracting signed-distance functions from multiview images. The abstract does not provide trajectory-error metrics or a head-to-head comparison with every conventional physics engine. Its contribution is scalable learned simulation with implicit shapes, supported by large-scene and image-derived demonstrations.

neurips-2024-learning-structure-aware-re.tldr: A detailed Agda proof dataset supports structural neural representations and improved premise selection.
paragraphs: Dependently typed programs encode rich relationships between expressions, types, and proofs. This paper brings Agda program-proofs into machine-learning research through a newly released dataset detailed enough to expose proof states at the subtype level.

The authors use that structure to design a neural architecture representing dependently typed programs through their organization rather than primarily through names. The high-resolution dataset enables learning from fine-grained proof information that would be lost in a coarse text-only description.

An evaluation on premise selection shows promising results that surpass strong baselines. The abstract does not state dataset size, numerical accuracy, or performance on complete automated proof construction. The contribution is both a resource connecting Agda with machine learning and an initial structural modeling method, with evidence on the specific task of choosing useful premises.

neurips-2024-llamo-large-language-model-.tldr: LLaMo connects molecular graphs to language-model instruction following through multilevel graph tokens.
paragraphs: Instruction-tuned language models have broad text capabilities, but molecular graphs require representations that do not naturally match ordinary language tokens. LLaMo is an end-to-end molecular graph-language assistant designed to connect those modalities.

A multilevel graph projector gathers representations from different graph-neural-network layers and molecular motifs, using cross-attention to form graph tokens. Machine-generated molecular instructions then support tuning for molecule-related language and prediction tasks.

Experiments report the best performance among the evaluated methods on molecular description generation, property prediction, and IUPAC-name prediction. The abstract does not provide scores or assess laboratory validation of generated claims. The contribution is a graph-to-language architecture plus instruction data and task evaluations, rather than evidence that the assistant can reliably determine every chemical property or replace experimental characterization.

neurips-2024-marrying-causal-representat.tldr: Identifiable causal representations and differentiable dynamics solvers combine into controllable scientific models.
paragraphs: Causal representation learning offers identifiability theory, while learned dynamical systems offer scalable modeling of trajectories. This paper connects their assumptions so that identifiable latent modeling can use practical differentiable differential-equation solvers.

The resulting models isolate parameters specific to each trajectory and make them explicitly controllable. Those parameters can support downstream tasks such as out-of-distribution classification and treatment-effect estimation, linking representation learning to questions beyond trajectory prediction alone.

Experiments include a wind simulator with partially known factors and real climate data. On the climate application, the model answers downstream causal questions consistently with existing literature. The abstract does not specify those questions or numerical validation. Its contribution is a practical bridge under stated modeling assumptions; agreement with prior findings is supporting evidence, not a general proof that every learned dynamical parameter has a causal interpretation.

neurips-2024-neural-collapse-inspired-fe.tldr: Neural-collapse-inspired masks align semantic features across learned environments to reduce background shortcuts.
paragraphs: Image classifiers can rely on backgrounds that happen to correlate with labels in training, then fail when those correlations change. This paper uses neural-collapse geometry to encourage class-relevant representations that remain consistent across environments.

The method alternates between assigning examples to environments and learning semantic masks. Local environment models and maximum-likelihood probabilities guide assignment. After masking the input, representations are encouraged to collapse toward the same simplex equiangular tight frame in every environment.

Experiments on four datasets show substantial improvements in out-of-distribution performance. The abstract does not identify the datasets, quantify gains, or prove complete separation of semantic and spurious information. The contribution is a shared geometric target coupled with learned environment structure, providing an evaluated way to discourage background-dependent shortcuts without claiming that all correlations are harmful or fully removable.

neurips-2024-online-learning-of-delayed-.tldr: Confidence-based online choice learning handles delayed feedback with near-optimal regret guarantees.
paragraphs: Sellers choosing products or advertisements must learn customers’ preferences from observed choices. When that feedback arrives late, decisions are made with incomplete information. This paper studies unknown multinomial-logit choice parameters in an online setting with delayed observations.

The proposed algorithm balances exploration and exploitation through confidence bounds and optimism. The authors first analyze a censored setting where a business-imposed threshold determines which delayed feedback is considered, obtaining regret of roughly O(sqrt(NT)) with a matching lower bound up to logarithmic factors.

They then extend the analysis to delays without that threshold and retain the same stated regret order. Experiments confirm effectiveness, although the abstract provides no numerical outcomes or complete delay assumptions. The guarantees belong to the specified choice model and feedback regimes, not every recommendation problem with arbitrarily missing or adversarially delayed responses.

neurips-2024-plip-language-image-pre-tra.tldr: PLIP adds person-specific attributes and identity supervision to language-image pretraining.
paragraphs: General language-image pretraining may overlook the fine-grained attributes and identities needed for person-centered tasks. PLIP designs its pretraining around those characteristics, aiming to produce representations better suited to matching and analyzing people across images and descriptions.

Three pretext tasks align text with image-region colors, predict attributes from images, and contrast visual and language representations at the identity level. The authors construct SYNTH-PEDES by automatically generating textual annotations for a large person-image dataset, then use it to pretrain the model.

Evaluation across person-centric downstream tasks shows improvements over existing methods and strong zero-shot and domain-generalization behavior. The abstract does not list task scores or analyze annotation error. The contribution is targeted representation learning and a paired dataset; its evidence concerns the evaluated recognition tasks rather than a general guarantee of accurate or unbiased person understanding.

neurips-2024-predicting-label-distributi.tldr: Ternary annotations let annotators express uncertainty when learning label distributions.
paragraphs: An example can relate to several labels by different degrees, but collecting a precise label distribution is costly. Binary annotations are easier, yet force a decision even when relevance is ambiguous. This paper adds a third option so uncertainty can be recorded explicitly.

Labels take values 1 for definitely relevant, -1 for definitely irrelevant, and 0 for uncertain relevance. A categorical model with monotonicity and ordering properties connects description degrees to these annotations, serving either as a loss or as a probability model that adapts existing label-enhancement methods.

The authors compare approximation errors theoretically and demonstrate effectiveness experimentally. The abstract does not provide numerical gains or establish that ternary labeling is preferable under every annotation process. The contribution is a learning formulation that preserves an expert’s uncertainty instead of requiring an unreliable binary judgment before inferring the richer label distribution.

neurips-2024-proedit-simple-progression-.tldr: ProEdit improves 3D editing consistency by breaking a large edit into progressive subtasks.
paragraphs: Diffusion-guided three-dimensional editing can produce inconsistent views because the image generator has many possible outputs. ProEdit reduces that ambiguity by decomposing a requested edit into smaller changes and applying them progressively to the scene.

A difficulty-aware scheduler chooses the subtask decomposition, while an adaptive three-dimensional Gaussian-splatting training strategy carries out each step efficiently. The framework lets users preview intermediate results and choose how aggressively to apply the edit as it progresses.

Extensive evaluations across scenes and challenging edits report state-of-the-art results without expensive added components or elaborate auxiliary training procedures. The abstract does not supply quality scores, timings, or a formal consistency guarantee. Its contribution is the progressive editing strategy and supporting scheduler, with evidence that controlling the scope of each change can improve the final multiview result.

neurips-2024-rl-on-incorrect-synthetic-d.tldr: Step-aware training on incorrect synthetic solutions improves math-reasoning data efficiency.
paragraphs: Synthetic correct solutions can improve mathematical reasoning, but more positive examples may also amplify spurious patterns. This paper studies when generated training data help and finds that correct solutions sampled from the fine-tuned learner itself can double the efficiency of the same synthetic problems.

The authors then incorporate responses judged incorrect by a final-answer verifier. These negatives must be constructed so training can recover the utility of individual intermediate steps, distinguishing useful reasoning from the parts that led to failure.

This step-aware scheme gives consistent improvements over positive-only training, reaching performance comparable to using eight times as much synthetic data. The authors connect it to advantage-weighted reinforcement learning and show it can undo spurious correlations learned from positives. The abstract does not claim arbitrary wrong answers are useful; the per-step construction is central to the reported benefit.

neurips-2024-saullm-54b-saullm-141b-scal.tldr: SaulLM scales legal-domain adaptation with continued pretraining, legal instructions, and preference alignment.
paragraphs: This paper adapts large Mixtral-based language models to legal text through continued pretraining, specialized instruction following, and alignment with human preferences about legal interpretations. The legal pretraining corpus contains more than 400 billion tokens.

Synthetic data support the instruction and alignment stages. The abstract describes model families with 54 billion and 140 billion parameters, while the supplied title names SaulLM-141B for the larger version. That naming discrepancy is present in the source and should be resolved through the linked paper or release details.

The models outperform previous open-source comparisons on LegalBench Instruct, and base, instruction-tuned, and aligned versions are released under the MIT License. The abstract does not give benchmark scores or evidence of reliable legal advice in practice. The contribution is domain adaptation at larger scale and analysis of its tradeoffs, with evaluation on a legal-language benchmark.
